summary: Working in linguistics and Indology, Manasi Dilip Nadkarni completed doctoral studies under Shyam Sundar Bhattacharya and held an appointment as a Research Scholar / Fellow at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

Specializing in religious and Buddhist studies, Manfred B. Steger studied at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa and Rutgers University, later holding professorships at Illinois State University, RMIT University, and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa.

An Indologist, linguist, and scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, Manfred Mayrhofer earned his Ph.D. and Habilitation at the University of Graz under Wilhelm Brandenstein, later holding full professorships at Saarland University and the University of Vienna.

Specializing in Tibetology and Iranian and Central Asian studies, Manfred Taube studied at the University of Leipzig under Friedrich Weller, where he later served as Professor of Tibetan and Mongolian Philology in 1991.
Mannudeva was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Bālakṛṣṇa Pāyaguṇḍa (Bala Sharman Payagunde).

A scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy, Manshi Kiyozawa studied at Ikuei Kyōkō and the University of Tokyo under Ernest Fenollosa. He served as the first dean and founding president of Otani University from 1901 to 1902.
Manu Leumann was an Indologist and linguist who held academic posts at the University of Munich (~1922–1927) and the University of Zurich (~1927–1959).

An archaeologist, Indologist, and Central Asian scholar, Marc Aurel Stein earned his PhD at Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth. He led Oriental College and served as an Archaeological Surveyor and Superintendent with the Archaeological Survey of India.
Marc Tiefenauer is an Indologist who completed his PhD at the University of Lausanne in 2016, studying under Johannes Bronkhorst and Nahid Rouzbeh.

Marc-Henri Deroche is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed his doctoral studies under Matthew T. Kapstein and was also taught by Fernand Meyer, Samten Gyaltsen Karmay, and Katsumi Mimaki, among others.

A linguist who studied under Antoine Meillet and Sylvain Lévi, Marcel Cohen held long-term academic appointments at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1911–1954) and the University of Paris (~1919–1954).

A scholar of Sinology, religion, and history, Marcel Granet studied under Émile Durkheim and Édouard Chavannes. He was a professor at INALCO and the Institut des Hautes Études Chinoises, as well as a directeur d'études at EPHE.
Marcel Griaule studied at INALCO and the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Marcel Mauss and Marcel Cohen before serving on the faculty at the University of Paris from ~1940 to 1956.

Specializing in sociology, religion, and Indology, Marcel Mauss studied under Émile Durkheim, Sylvain Lévi, and others. He served as Directeur d’études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and held the Chair of Sociology at Collège de France.

A scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Marcelle Lalou studied under Sylvain Lévi and Jacques Bacot at EPHE, where she obtained her doctorate. She taught at EPHE from 1938 to 1963 and served as chief editor of Journal Asiatique.
Marco Walther is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed his PhD at the University of Munich under the supervision of Franz-Karl Ehrhard.

Working in Buddhist studies and computational methods, Marcus Bingenheimer studied at Nagoya University and the University of Würzburg. He held posts at the Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts, Chung-Hwa Institute, and Temple University.

A scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, Marek Mejor held the Michael Coulson Junior Research Fellowship at Wolfson College, Oxford (1981–1982) and later served as a professor at the University of Warsaw (attested 2000–2010).
A scholar of Buddhist and religious studies, Marek Zemánek studied at Seoul National University, Dongguk University, and Charles University, where he completed his dissertation under Radek Chlup.
Marek Zvelebil was an archaeologist who studied at the University of Sheffield (~1972–1976) and later held an academic post there from ~1981 to 2011.
